$comment: Design tokens — the single source of truth for both client languages. Angular consumes the generated CSS custom properties; Flutter consumes the generated Dart. Edit this file, never the generated output.
$structure: Two layers. `color`, `space`, `radius`, `font`, `shadow` and `motion` are primitives — raw values with no opinion about where they are used. `theme.light` and `theme.dark` are the semantic layer: they name a job (surface, border, text-muted) and point at a primitive. Components must only ever use the semantic layer, because that is what makes dark mode a token swap rather than a rewrite. A component that reaches for --color-brand-500 directly is a component that will be unreadable in one theme.
$brand: Green #08911F and gold #D2CC06, taken from the live platform: customers already recognise the colour, it is on the app store listings and the printed material, and a rebuild that arrives in a different green reads as a different company. The type is not carried over. Poppins was doing two jobs — poster headline and 13px table cell — and was interesting at neither; Clash Display and General Sans split them.

color.$neutral: Biased a few degrees toward the brand's green rather than a pure grey. A pure mid-grey next to a saturated green reads as unconsidered; the bias is small enough that nobody names it and large enough that the page feels like one palette.
color.$semantic: Danger is deliberately not the brand colour. The live platform sets --ion-color-danger to the same green as --ion-color-primary, so a destructive confirmation and a primary action are the same button — that is a bug worth not carrying over.

radius.$comment: Sharp, and in three jobs. A control (button, input, chip inside a field) is 4px, a card is 6px, and what floats above the page (a dialog, a drawer, a sheet, a menu) is 8px, so a control inside a card inside a sheet still steps up. The t-shirt steps are the same values under the names components already use: md is a control, lg is a card, xl is an overlay. Anything past 8px reads as a consumer app from 2019, and the product looked softer than the money moving through it.

font.$family: Two faces, self-hosted as woff2 rather than linked from a font service. Clash Display carries headings, prices and the one number a screen is about; General Sans does everything a person reads rather than looks at. Both from Fontshare under the ITF Free Font Licence.

tracking.$comment: Display type is set tighter than UI type. At 36px and up, default spacing reads as loose and slightly cheap; at 13px in a table it reads as legible, which is the job there.

$shadow: Layered rather than single, and tinted with the brand hue rather than pure black. One blurred shadow reads as a smudge under a card; a tight contact shadow with a wider ambient one above it reads as a card sitting on a surface, which is the whole difference between a flat page and one with a hierarchy. Dark mode carries a hairline of light along the top edge instead, because a shadow on a near-black ground is invisible and the edge is what separates the card from what is behind it.

light.$field-border: Separate from border-strong because the requirement is different. A divider is decoration; the edge of an input is how somebody knows there is an input there, and WCAG 1.4.11 puts that at 3:1. Reusing the decorative border here measures 1.67:1 — visible to whoever designed it on a good monitor, and not to anyone else.
light.$text-subtle: A step darker than neutral-500, which stays as the field edge. The 500 measured 4.62:1 on white and so passed where it was checked, but hints are written on the page ground and on insets as often as on cards: 4.33:1 on the footer's ground, 3.99:1 as a select's empty value. #646c64 keeps 4.5:1 on all three.
light.$primary: brand-600 rather than the brand 500 as the interactive fill. White on #08911f measures 4.13:1, which is under WCAG AA for the 14px semibold a button label actually is. The hue is unchanged — the step moves, which is what a brand colour is a ramp for.
light.$shadow-card: Every card sits on the page with a visible lift: a contact shadow and a wider ambient one beneath it. The 1px contact shadow alone left a card reading as a rectangle with a line under it. shadow-lift is the same card under a pointer, for anything that leads somewhere.
light.$scarce: The badges that say how much is left: "Almost sold out" and "Only 4 left" in the warm warning ramp, "Sold out" in near-black. Their own roles rather than warning and text, because they sit on posters as often as on cards, and a badge must read on a photograph of anything — so each is a solid fill with its own label colour, checked as a pair.

theme.$dark: Not an inversion. The brand green at #08911f is too dark to read on a dark ground, so the primary steps up to the 300 and its text goes dark green — the accent keeps working in both themes rather than being quietly illegible in one.

dark.$text-subtle: Lighter than the field edge it used to share: #7f887f was 4.47:1 on a card and 3.96:1 on an inset. #8d968d keeps 4.5:1 on every dark surface a hint is written on.
